annotation.method: Codex read the complete local paper, surveyed all definitions, lemmas, theorems, derived stability conclusions, and the row-pivoting counterexample, rejected externally delegated or asymptotic-only candidates, searched the frozen mathlib and NumStability baselines, visually checked every selected source page, and compiled private N/L proofs before accepting the targets.
annotation.reason: The project owner assigned the P08 source selection and benchmark annotation to Codex.

corpus_membership: This paper is part of the current corpus listed in metadata/manifest.json.
paper_version: published journal version; volume 35, issue 151, July 1980, printed pages 817-832

rejected_candidates.candidate: the three stability definitions in section 2
rejected_candidates.reason: These introduce backward-error measures and stability terminology rather than proving finite conclusions.
The result is explicitly attributed to Oettli and Prager (1964), and its proof is delegated to prior work.

Their existential perturbation constructions depend on continuity across poles, infima, absolute norms, and explicit matrix inverses. The selected tasks retain the paper's later iterative-refinement contributions with more direct finite source anchors.

rejected_candidates.candidate: the basic Gaussian-elimination error estimate and equation (3.1)
rejected_candidates.reason: The basic estimate is taken from Skeel (1979); equation (3.1) is background used by the new refinement analysis.

Its printed constants depend on the externally supplied Gaussian-elimination estimate and several anonymous dimension-dependent matrices. T3 isolates the exact recurrence and induction step that Lemma 4.1 feeds.
The theorem is a direct substitution of Lemma 4.3 into Lemma 4.2 and contains many anonymous constants; T2 and T3 preserve those two mathematically distinct ingredients exactly.
These use informal limits and anonymous constants; the finite recurrence certificate in T3 avoids an unstated convergence formalization.
The displayed bounds are explicitly derived from external theorems in Jankowski and Wozniakowski (1977).

The full formulas combine anonymous constants, asymptotic interpretation, and Theorems 2.2 and 4.4. The selected Lemma 4.2 and Lemma 4.3 tasks retain the exact finite iterative-refinement ingredients without encoding O(u^2).
The counterexample text is partially degraded in the supplied scan and the surrounding row-pivoting bounds are stated as straightforward modifications rather than separately proved results.

rejected_candidates.candidate: the unlabelled introductory one-refinement identity on printed page 825
rejected_candidates.reason: It is a faithful finite identity after exposing the solve perturbation, but the closest IterativeRefinement theorem is not present in the frozen condition-L object bundle. It therefore cannot honestly serve as the direct-use target; Lemma 4.2 supplies an exact frozen-bundle-compatible T1 instead.

T1.decision: Use the forward-error half of Lemma 4.2 in expanded finite-sum form.

T2.decision: Use the residual-image half of Lemma 4.2, which combines inverse action, matrix additivity, and two componentwise bounds.

T3.decision: Use Lemma 4.3's signed affine recurrence and induction as an exact finite matrix-geometric bound.

selection_policy: Use a finite claim made and proved in this paper.
Reject definitions, experiments, vague asymptotics, and claims whose proof is mainly delegated elsewhere.
Prefer exact displayed bounds, identities, and the finite recurrence behind an induction.
Keep the fixed Lean setting condition-neutral and paper-scoped.
Assign tiers only after verified frozen-library searches.
